concerns.text: Task T001 only verifies that the fetched dataset contains ≥ 1 species (test asserts species count ≥ 1). This weakens FR-001, which mandates at least 50 paired plant species. The task must enforce the ≥ 50 species requirement and fail if not met.

Task T003’s verification accepts any number of significant metabolite classes (≥ 1) and merely documents a null result. This weakens FR-003, which requires identification of exactly 3‑5 metabolite classes with significant negative correlation. The task must enforce the 3‑5 range and flag a failure otherwise.

Task T004’s verification only checks that R² > 0.1 (or documents if lower), whereas SC-002 specifies a threshold of R² > 0.3. This relaxes the success criterion and must be tightened to the > 0.3 requirement.
Task T004 logs a warning if any VIF ≥ 5 but does not treat it as a failure. SC-004 requires VIF < 5; the task should enforce this as a hard constraint, not a soft warning.

Task T004 uses a single 80/20 train‑test split, violating Constitution VII which mandates k‑fold (k=5) cross‑validation for model validation. The OLS implementation must adopt 5‑fold CV and report the required metrics.
Task T005 fits PGLS and mixed‑effects models without any cross‑validation, also breaching Constitution VII’s k‑fold CV requirement for all predictive models.

Task T007’s sensitivity analysis re‑runs OLS and Random Forest on raw (non‑standardized) metabolite concentrations, directly contradicting Constitution VI which mandates that all modeling use z‑score‑standardized data.

Task T010’s report template allows omission of negative findings (e.g., “If a placeholder dataset was used…”) without mandating explicit statement of any failure to meet FR‑001 or SC‑001. This can lead to silent weakening of acceptance criteria; the report must explicitly note when sample‑size or power criteria are unmet.

Task T012’s handoff document does not require the paper‑stage team to verify that all acceptance criteria (e.g., ≥ 50 species, R² > 0.3, VIF < 5) have been satisfied before inclusion in the manuscript, risking downstream omission of unmet constraints.
